name: Govern UTM parameters and naming across every paid channel
what: Extend the Meta naming convention to a single UTM and naming schema shared by Meta, Google, TikTok, affiliate links and email so every paid click lands in analytics under one consistent source, medium, campaign and content field.
encompasses: define one UTM schema (source, medium, campaign, content, term) that all platforms and the affiliate network fill the same way
audit live campaigns for missing, duplicate or inconsistent UTMs
generate correct UTM strings at campaign build time instead of after launch
flag affiliate and creator links that bypass the schema and would misattribute in GA4 or the warehouse
keep a lookup table mapping platform campaign IDs to the naming convention for the daily read
catch naming drift when a human edits a campaign name inside Ads Manager or Google Ads UI
inputs: existing campaign and ad set names
GA4 or warehouse channel grouping rules
outputs: UTM and naming standard document
a drift report naming every non-conforming live campaign or link
trigger: new campaign build, or a scheduled weekly naming audit
tools: spreadsheet or script for UTM audit
founder_sees: the drift report and the schema once, then only exceptions

name: Run dynamic creative optimisation and asset-group combinatorial testing
what: Go beyond setting a volume and refresh target: build the structured headline, image, video and CTA combinations that Advantage+ Shopping, PMax asset groups and TikTok Smart+ actually mix at delivery time, and read which combination elements (not just whole ads) are carrying performance.
encompasses: group creative assets into the components a DCO or asset-group system recombines (hooks, body images, CTAs, headlines)
size the asset pool per component so the system has enough diversity to avoid repeating the same pairing
read Meta's and Google's asset-level performance reports to find which individual component is winning, not just which whole ad
retire a weak component without killing an otherwise strong ad
flag when a brand tone or claim would fail if machine-recombined with the wrong headline
feed the component-level read back into the next creative brief
outputs: component performance report
next-round creative brief with named components to keep, refresh or retire
trigger: after an asset group or Advantage+ campaign has enough delivery to read component data
founder_sees: the component report and any brand-safety flag on a recombination
human_role: paid social manager, performance marketing manager

name: Plan the India festive calendar into the peak sale ramp
what: Add India-specific festival windows (Diwali, Raksha Bandhan, Holi, Eid, Onam) and quick-commerce demand spikes to the peak sale ramp plan, since these carry different messaging, stock and payment behaviour than a generic sale.
encompasses: build a dated festival calendar for the brand's category with historical demand notes where available
map WhatsApp and messaging spend uplift around Diwali, since messaging engagement runs far above other channels in that window
flag GST invoice and advance-payment timing for pre-festival stock loans as a founder-visible dependency, not a media task
size quick-commerce ad spend separately from Meta/Google for the festival window, since intent and basket size differ
set the wind-down date and post-festival RTO watch, since COD orders spike and RTO risk rises after a festival
outputs: festival ramp plan with dated budget and creative milestones
trigger: 8 to 10 weeks before a known India festival window
founder_sees: the full ramp plan before any budget moves

name: Run a recurring ad account access and security hygiene review
what: Beyond the initial access and ownership setup, run a standing quarterly (or on-trigger) review that every asset is still owned by the brand, every partner and admin still needs access, and 2FA is enforced everywhere, then produces an offboarding list.
encompasses: list every admin, partner and app connected to the ad account, Page, pixel, catalog and Business Manager
flag any admin or partner with access but no active work in the last 90 days
confirm 2FA (or Meta Protect equivalent) is enforced on every admin login, not just the primary
confirm asset ownership sits with the brand and agencies hold partner access only, never ownership
produce a one-click offboarding list when an agency or freelancer relationship ends
verify the named account and customer IDs in internal records still match the live account
inputs: Business Manager / MCC admin and partner list
vendor and freelancer roster with start/end dates
outputs: access hygiene report with a stale-access and offboarding list
trigger: quarterly, or when a vendor or freelancer relationship ends

external_write.surface: Meta Business Manager / Google Ads MCC admin settings

founder_sees: the full report; founder approves every access removal
human_role: ads account manager at an agency, ad ops

name: Run Meta and cross-platform creator whitelisting with a rights and expiry registry
what: Extend the TikTok Spark loop to Meta Partnership Ads (formerly branded content ads) and any other platform's paid-partnership feature, and keep one registry of every creator's usage rights, authorization window and expiry so no ad runs on lapsed permission.

record, per creator asset, the platforms licensed, the usage window, whitelisting fee and whether paid distribution rights were bought or only organic
flag any live ad running on a creator authorization that has expired or was never granted
separate whitelisting spend and results from the brand's own-handle ads in reporting, since delivery and cost behave differently
keep a renewal reminder ahead of every authorization expiry
inputs: Meta Partnership Ads and TikTok Spark authorization status
outputs: creator rights and expiry registry
expiry alerts
whitelisting performance split from owned-handle ads
trigger: on creator onboarding, and continuously for expiry watch

external_write.surface: Meta Partnership Ads tagging, TikTok Spark authorization

name: Produce the client-facing monthly paid media report
what: Beyond the internal daily and weekly read, produce the narrative, board-ready monthly deck an agency account manager sends a client: what happened, why, what changed, and what is asked for next month.
encompasses: summarise the month's blended MER, per-platform ROAS, spend and the biggest single change from last month
write the plain-language narrative behind the numbers (why a metric moved), not just the numbers
list what was tested, what won, what was killed, with the evidence
state the budget or decision being asked of the client for next month
keep every number recomputed from the metric contract, never restated from a platform screenshot

outputs: a monthly client report (deck or document)

name: Manage the affiliate and creator partner program end to end
what: Run the affiliate program the way an affiliate manager does: recruit, vet and approve or reject applicants, ship assets and terms, monitor active partners, and keep the program healthy without a human touching each application.
encompasses: screen inbound affiliate applications against a fixed rule set (site quality, traffic source, category fit, prior brand mentions)
auto-approve applicants that clearly pass, auto-reject clear spam or bad-fit, and route only the borderline cases to the founder
generate each approved affiliate's tracking link, coupon code and starter asset kit
send onboarding messages and respond to routine affiliate questions (commission rate, cookie window, allowed channels) from a fixed FAQ
flag dormant affiliates (no clicks or sales in 60 days) for reactivation or removal
keep a running leaderboard of active affiliates by revenue and conversion rate

affiliate network data (Everflow, Impact, Refersion or similar)
outputs: approve/reject decisions with reasons
onboarding kit per affiliate
dormant-affiliate list
leaderboard

name: Detect and block affiliate and coupon fraud
what: Watch affiliate and coupon activity for the patterns that steal commission or margin without earning it: too-fast click-to-conversion, suspect ISPs, brand-bidding on paid search, and coupon codes leaked to public deal sites.
encompasses: flag conversions that complete in under the platform's normal minimum time from click to purchase (a common fraud signature)
flag traffic clusters from data-centre or proxy ISPs rather than real consumer connections
search for the brand's affiliate coupon codes appearing on public coupon-aggregator sites the affiliate was never given rights to post on
flag an affiliate bidding on the brand's own name in Google Ads to intercept traffic that would have converted for free
hold commission on flagged conversions pending founder review instead of auto-paying
inputs: affiliate network click and conversion logs
outputs: fraud flag list with evidence per flagged affiliate
held-commission list
trigger: continuous on the affiliate network's event stream, or a weekly scan
tools: affiliate network fraud data (none connected yet)
founder_sees: every flagged affiliate before commission is withheld or the affiliate is suspended

name: Design commission tiers and reconcile affiliate payouts
what: Set commission rates by partner type, product category and customer status (new vs returning), then reconcile what the affiliate network says is owed against actual delivered orders before any payout goes out.
encompasses: propose a commission schedule split by partner type (content, coupon, loyalty, influencer) and by new-vs-returning customer
recompute owed commission from the brand's own order data, not just the network's claimed conversions
flag any mismatch between network-reported and order-confirmed sales before payout
hold commission on an order that is later returned, cancelled or RTO'd, and net it out of the next payout cycle
surface the true net cost of the affiliate channel (commission plus discount) against its incremental revenue
outputs: proposed commission schedule
reconciled payout file
true net-cost read of the channel
trigger: each payout cycle, and whenever a tier change is proposed
founder_sees: every commission schedule change and every payout file before it is sent

name: Prepare Amazon and Flipkart marketplace ad briefs for handoff
what: Since marketplace ad platforms sit outside the agent's connected accounts, prepare the full Sponsored Products/Brands (Amazon) and sponsored placement (Flipkart) plan as a brief a human or agency executes inside the marketplace's own ads console.
encompasses: pull the bestseller and margin data needed to pick which SKUs get sponsored placement first
propose keyword targets from the brand's own Google Search terms that already convert, plus marketplace search suggestions
build the negative keyword list to exclude irrelevant marketplace searches
propose ACOS or TACOS targets from the SKU's actual margin, not a generic benchmark
propose a budget split across search, product-page and brand-store placements
flag catalogue or listing issues (missing bullet points, weak images) that will cap ad performance before spend starts
inputs: brand's own Google Search converting terms
outputs: a marketplace ad campaign brief ready to build inside Amazon Seller Central or Flipkart Ads Manager
trigger: before a marketplace ad launch or a quarterly marketplace ads review
founder_sees: the full brief before it is handed to whoever executes it

name: Prepare quick commerce retail media briefs for Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart
what: Prepare a self-serve retail media plan for India's quick-commerce ad platforms, since a user with active purchase intent behaves differently from a social scroller and the ad platforms are outside the agent's connected accounts.
encompasses: check which quick-commerce platforms the brand's SKUs are actually listed and in-stock on before proposing spend
propose which SKUs to sponsor based on category search volume on that platform and current margin
propose a budget sized to the platform's own reported category benchmarks, since CPCs and ROAS norms differ from Meta or Google
flag stockout risk before scaling, since quick-commerce ad delivery can outpace local dark-store inventory
keep quick-commerce ad results separate from Meta/Google in reporting, since attribution windows and intent differ
inputs: quick-commerce listing and stock status per dark store or city
outputs: a retail media brief per platform ready for a human to execute in the platform's brand console
trigger: before a quick-commerce ad push, or when the brand adds a new quick-commerce listing

name: Evaluate and brief programmatic display and DSP retargeting options
what: When Meta and Google retargeting pools are saturated, evaluate whether a DSP (Criteo, RTB House, Trade Desk, Amazon DSP) is worth adding, and if so prepare the creative-spec and audience brief, since the agent has no DSP connector.
encompasses: check whether the brand's retargeting pool is actually saturated (frequency and reach data) before recommending a new channel
compare DSP options by data source fit (shopping data vs streaming vs marketplace-native) against the brand's category
estimate minimum spend and management fee against expected incremental reach
specify the creative sizes and dynamic feed format the chosen DSP needs
flag brand-safety and cookie-deprecation considerations specific to programmatic display
inputs: current retargeting pool size and frequency
budget available for a new channel
outputs: a go/no-go recommendation with a DSP shortlist and a creative-spec brief if go

founder_sees: the recommendation before any DSP is contacted

name: Track and resolve ad policy rejections and account quality across platforms
what: Log every ad disapproval and account-quality flag from Meta, Google and TikTok, diagnose the actual policy clause it hit, fix the copy or asset, and draft the appeal text, rather than treating each rejection as a one-off surprise.
encompasses: pull every disapproved ad and its stated policy reason on a daily check
map the stated reason to the specific policy clause and the likely real cause (claim, image text ratio, restricted category wording, landing page mismatch)
propose the smallest edit that fixes the violation without changing the offer or claim tier
draft the appeal text for a rejection the agent believes was wrongly applied, for a human to submit
watch the account-quality or account-health score and flag a downward trend before it causes a restriction
keep a running log of rejection reasons by category to catch a pattern (e.g. one claim type failing repeatedly)
inputs: platform disapproval reasons and account-quality dashboards
outputs: daily rejection log with cause and fix
appeal drafts
account-quality trend flag
trigger: any new ad disapproval, or a daily account-quality check

name: Evaluate and configure a third-party attribution or MMM stack
what: Decide whether a paid attribution/MMM tool (Triple Whale, Northbeam, Rockerbox or similar) is worth its cost versus the brand's own blended-MER and lift-test approach, and if adopted, configure it correctly rather than trusting its default setup.
encompasses: compare what each tool actually measures (multi-touch attribution, MMM, incrementality) against what the brand's open question is
estimate the tool's monthly cost against the decision quality it would add over the existing MER and lift-test process
specify the correct first-party pixel and post-purchase survey setup if the tool is adopted, so it is not fed bad data
cross-check the tool's attributed ROAS against platform-reported ROAS and blended MER before trusting any of its numbers
flag when a tool's built-in recommendation (e.g. auto budget shifts) would touch a live account and needs the same founder gate as any other write
outputs: a go/no-go recommendation with setup checklist if adopted

founder_sees: the recommendation before any tool is purchased or connected

name: Reconcile ad platform billing and invoices against the budget ledger
what: Match what Meta, Google and TikTok actually billed (invoices, credits, GST/RCM) against platform-reported spend and the brand's own budget ledger, since these three numbers routinely disagree.
encompasses: pull each platform's monthly invoice and match it line by line against the platform's own reported spend for that period
flag invalid-traffic or ad-credit refunds that land on a later invoice and would otherwise look like a discrepancy
check GST/RCM treatment on foreign ad platform invoices (Meta, Google, TikTok bill from outside India) against what was actually remitted
flag a GSTIN-to-billing-address mismatch that would make an input tax credit invalid
post the reconciled true cost, not the platform's self-reported spend, into the budget ledger
flag a payment-method failure or credit-line limit before it pauses live campaigns
outputs: monthly reconciliation report
ledger entries reflecting true billed cost
GST/RCM discrepancy flags
trigger: monthly on invoice receipt, or when platform-reported spend and card charges diverge
founder_sees: the full reconciliation and any GST mismatch

name: Allocate budget across channels by marginal ROAS
what: Compare the marginal (next-dollar) return of Meta, Google, TikTok and any retail media channel against each other, not just each channel's own average ROAS, and propose where the next dollar of budget should go.
encompasses: compute marginal ROAS per channel from the spend/revenue curve over the last N days, not the average ROAS
flag a channel that looks profitable on average but whose marginal return has turned poor (past its saturation point)
weigh marginal ROAS against attribution confidence, audience saturation, creative fatigue and stock constraints before proposing a shift
propose a bounded shift (a percentage cap per period) rather than a full reallocation, to avoid resetting any platform's learning phase
separate a proposed shift due to real headroom from one due to a broken tracking signal
outputs: a ranked budget-shift proposal with the marginal ROAS evidence per channel

name: Set guardrails and audit logs for platform-native agentic bidding features
what: Meta, Google and TikTok are shipping their own autonomous agents (Advantage+, PMax auto-everything, Google's Marketing Advisor, TikTok's agent protocol) that can act on an account with a permission grant. Before any of these is turned on, set the spend cap, performance floor and category exclusions, and keep an audit log of every autonomous action taken.
encompasses: read what a given platform's agentic feature is actually permitted to change (budget, bids, creative, targeting) before granting it any permission
set a hard spend cap and a performance floor (e.g. CPA ceiling) the feature cannot cross without a fresh approval
exclude brand-sensitive categories (health claims, kids, finance-adjacent) from any autonomous creative or targeting change
pull the platform's action log after every run and diff it against the guardrails to confirm nothing was crossed
revoke the permission the moment a guardrail is breached, rather than waiting for the next scheduled review

brand spend caps and performance floors
outputs: a guardrail configuration
a run-by-run audit log with any breach flagged
trigger: before turning on any platform-native autonomous feature, and after every run

draft a personalised outreach message referencing the specific post found and proposing whitelisting terms

name: Fan out a media anomaly to site, stock and competitor data for root cause

encompasses: on any flagged anomaly, pull that day's site speed measurement, stock levels for the affected SKUs and any logged competitor discount or ad surge

distinguish a demand-side cause (stockout, site down, competitor discount) from a platform-side cause (delivery, auction, tracking break)
state plainly when none of the available signals explain the anomaly, rather than forcing a guess
attach the ranked causes to the same anomaly report the daily read already produces

trigger: every time a spend/ROAS anomaly is flagged
founder_sees: the anomaly report with its ranked causes
